context.purpose: Inspect an Oracle schema, load captured typed rows, publish exact relational reports and run atomic mutation transactions, each verified independently from a fresh connection.
context.assumptions: A dedicated Python interpreter with python-oracledb (Thin mode) and a host-held connection profile (SCHEMAXIS_ORACLE_<PROFILE>_USER, _PASSWORD, _DSN environment variables). AL32UTF8 database; BOOLEAN needs Oracle Database 23 or later. The adaptor works in the connected schema.
context.constraints: 1-8 tables, 1-32 columns, up to 5000 rows per table and 4 MiB per source; NUMBER/VARCHAR2/DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE/RAW/BOOLEAN/CLOB/BLOB/native JSON; equi-joins, named null-aware conditions, bounded derived values, groups, windows and set operations; at most 10000 result rows. LOB cells are bounded to 262144 UTF-16 code units/bytes, JSON text to 262144 UTF-8 bytes; JSON scalar paths use member/index steps. No authored SQL, PL/SQL, packages, vectors or administration.
context.inspection: Compare report.json/report.csv, snapshot.json, load-summary.json or transaction.json/state-after.json with the retained identify/apply/readback evidence; the verifier recomputes every expected row with an independent Decimal/datetime reference and compares the fresh-connection readback.
context.recovery: ORACLE_CREDENTIALS_MISSING: export the named variables. ORACLE_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED/ORACLE_UNAVAILABLE: check the profile values and listener; nothing was changed. INVALID_ORACLE_TABLE/QUERY/TRANSACTION/VALUE/SOURCE: read the location and observed reason. ORACLE_OBJECT_EXISTS: choose a free name; tables are never replaced. ORACLE_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION/ORACLE_ROWCOUNT_MISMATCH: the transaction was rolled back (observed.rollbackVerified). ORACLE_SERIALIZATION_CONFLICT: inspect current state and ledger, then make a fresh explicit attempt; provision external ledgers with SEGMENT CREATION IMMEDIATE. ORACLE_COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN: never rerun; inspect first. INCOMPLETE_EXECUTION: fix the recorded faultCode and run in a fresh directory.

workflow.scope: Verified report.json values and report.csv tables can feed downstream declared workflow fields; table definitions can be reused across operations with document references.

composition.scope: Shared references, closed expressions and finite visits resolve to the same literal typed contract.

lifecycle.timeout: One total deadline covers the identify, apply and readback worker stages and final verification; the connection call timeout bounds each database call.
lifecycle.cancellation: Shared owned-process-group cancellation; an abandoned session rolls back uncommitted work, and an unreadable COMMIT is reported as outcome unknown, never replayed.
lifecycle.logs: Retain authored/effective plans, captured sources, generated programs, per-stage submissions, stdout/stderr and fault records; credential values, DSNs and host names are redacted and the run directory is scanned for credential values.
lifecycle.verification: Independent literal Decimal/datetime/three-valued-logic reference for every report, constraint and mutation; fresh-connection dictionary and row readback; separate observer connection for uncommitted-invisible and post-finish state.

data.format: JSON row-object arrays or CSV with header
losses: NUMBER is exact decimal text; scale loss is refused unless scalePolicy is round. Empty text and empty RAW are NULL in Oracle and are refused unless emptyText is null.
No FLOAT, NCLOB/BFILE, interval, object, XML, spatial or vector values; DATE has whole seconds and no zone; TIMESTAMP is limited to six fractional digits; time zones are fixed numeric offsets.
data.scope: Each regular local source at most 4 MiB and 5000 rows; every column and key declared. Bounded CLOB/BLOB: non-empty Unicode/hex; native JSON: exact canonical standard JSON text.

traits.numbers: exact decimal text or exactly representable JSON numbers

losses: Rows are published in the declared order and, within ties, in canonical column order; ties across limit/offset are refused.
jsonNumber is refused when a value is not exactly representable as a double.
data.scope: Artifact index 0 is report.json (columns, rows); index 1 is report.csv.

losses: Check-constraint expressions, privileges, storage and partitioning are not part of the snapshot.
data.scope: Tables, columns, keys, indexes, views and sequences of the connected schema.

data.format: JSON transaction outcome and final table state

traits.states: before, in-transaction, observer and after states compared

losses: External tables require SERIALIZABLE, database enforcement and an idempotency ledger. Prospective validation and native row comparison occur before COMMIT. A failed COMMIT is never replayed.

inspection.scope: View report.json, report.csv, snapshot.json, load-summary.json, transaction.json and state-after.json.
inspection.limits: The database itself is not browsed; verification reads it through fresh connections.

authoring.reuse: Edit the example's tables and report/transaction fields in place; table declarations can be shared between operations with document references. Runs are never reused by input identity because live database state is not part of it.

native-inspection.scope: The adaptor does not implement native-inspection; edit declared inputs and execute a new verified run.

mpi.scope: The adaptor does not implement mpi; Oracle workflows are serial.

time-batches.scope: The adaptor does not implement time-batches; edit declared inputs and execute a new verified run.

live-editing.scope: The adaptor does not implement live-editing; edit declared inputs and execute a new verified run.

conversion.scope: The adaptor does not implement conversion; relational results are published as typed JSON and CSV only.

workflow.scope: Verified JSON values and CSV tables feed downstream declared workflow fields; load/inspect/report/mutate share table records with document references.

composition.scope: Shared references, closed expressions and finite visits resolve to the same literal typed contract.

reusable-inputs.scope: A live database's rows and schema change independently of the local source files, so no run is reusable by input identity; every execution re-runs. A rerun starts from captured sources and refuses (ORACLE_OBJECT_EXISTS) when its table names are taken, so a retained or interrupted earlier run must be inspected and removed first; an unknown commit outcome is never retried automatically.

source-authoring.scope: Edit table sources and declarations through shared JSON authoring and undo.

property-authoring.scope: Edit tables, relations, conditions, measures, windows and transaction steps through nested shared forms.

native-save.scope: load persists committed, independently reopened tables in the connected schema when setup.retain is true.

cases.scope: Left join, null-aware grouping and exact NUMBER sums over a fresh-connection-verified load; includes a NULL group key, a NULL total, a customer without orders and Unicode names.
Full outer join exposes an order without a customer in the NULL region group while the customer without orders adds no count.
Three-table join with CSV input including a timestamp-with-time-zone column, a derived product, HAVING and a rank window; hand-computed 2 x 25.05 + 50.00 = 100.10 and 10 x 25.04 = 250.40.
Row accounting after a fresh-connection readback of three created tables with keys and a cascade rule.
A snapshot restricted to a name that does not exist is empty and stable across two fresh connections.
Committed transfer with savepoint, insert and merge; observer connection sees nothing before the commit.
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT undoes an insert but keeps the earlier debit; serializable isolation.
A transaction that deletes every row and inserts another finishes by rolling back; the original rows remain.
Unicode CLOB beyond VARCHAR2 capacity, binary BLOB, native JSON and exact typed number/text/boolean extraction, including JSON null, missing members and empty scalar text.

completion.scope: Supported relational/document workflow scope: connection/identity, dictionary inspection and drift, exact scalar types, bounded CLOB/BLOB and native JSON with typed member/index extraction, table/constraint definitions, typed loading, relational reports, atomic mutation with prospective and precommit checks, external-table idempotency. These are partial Oracle capability families; schema evolution, PL/SQL, vector, advanced types, spatial/graph/text, AQ and other families remain visible in docs/design/oracle-coverage.md.
